title: Resume a vSAN Data Protection snapshot sweep across a session token expiry
prompt:
Implement the protection group snapshot sweep in src/SnapserviceSweepClient.java. It is a dependency-free, single-file Java client for the VCF 9.1 vSAN Data Protection snapshot appliance. The wire contract is pinned in docs/contract.json, derived from the vSAN Data Protection OpenAPI specification; docs/official_sources.json records where it came from. Only the four operations the contract names exist on this appliance: Snapservice.Sessions_create, Snapservice.Clusters.ProtectionGroups_list, Snapservice.Clusters.ProtectionGroups.Snapshots_create$Task and Snapservice.Tasks_get.

sweepCluster must take a one-time snapshot of every ACTIVE protection group in the cluster and wait for the results. Do it in three phases: list the ACTIVE protection groups once, then start a snapshot for each one, then poll every task until it reaches a terminal state. Snapshot names are namePrefix + "-" + protectionGroupIdentifier. A protection group listed in retentionByProtectionGroup is snapshotted with that retention period; one that is absent is snapshotted with none. Return the outcome for each protection group in listing order, along with how many sessions the client created.

A session token on this appliance can expire part way through a sweep. When it does, the appliance answers 401 and rejects the request before doing any work. Recover by re-authenticating and replaying exactly that one request unchanged with the new token, then carrying on. Work that already succeeded must not be lost or repeated: do not list the protection groups again, do not re-create a snapshot that was already accepted, and do not restart the sweep. Re-authenticate only in reaction to a 401 -- never refresh a token that has not actually been refused.

Send the exact request shape the contract specifies. Optional inputs that are not set must be omitted from the request, not sent as empty or null: an unset optional query parameter contributes nothing to the query string, and CreateSpec.retention is left out of the request body entirely when there is no retention period. Snapservice.Sessions_create authenticates with basic_auth and carries no session header or body; every other operation authenticates with the vmware-api-session-id header and sends no Authorization header.

Keep the existing public API and the single-file layout. docs/, tests/ and the mock appliance are fixed -- do not modify them. Run `python3 tests/verify.py` to check your work.
